Counterevidence checked: on ordinary uncloned linear TX skbs pskb_trim takes the __skb_trim fast path and the read stays in-bounds, so the issue is latent for common traffic; the function is TX (not remote RX), which narrows attacker control to locally generated or forwarded frames.

Untrusted source: batadv_recv_unicast_packet() is the rx handler for batman-adv unicast frames registered in batadv_rx_handler[] and dispatched from batadv_batman_skb_recv() (net/batman-adv/main.c:484), i.e. a ptype receive handler fed by eth_type_trans output; an attacker on the L2 segment can send ETH_P_BATMAN frames. Missing guarantee: on entry the only linear-area guarantee is batadv_batman_skb_recv()'s pskb_may_pull(skb, 2) (net/batman-adv/main.c:452), so with a non-linear skb (frags/frag_list from GRO or SG receive) only 2 bytes are guaranteed in the head, yet this function casts skb->data to struct batadv_unicast_packet and immediately reads unicast_packet->packet_type (offset 0, 1 byte, so this specific read is inside the 2-byte guarantee). The violated invariant is the pattern, but the single packet_type byte at offset 0 is actually within the 2 pulled bytes; however hdr_size is then chosen as sizeof(struct batadv_unicast_4addr_packet) (20 bytes) and later batadv_check_unicast_packet()/batadv_check_unicast_ttvn() pull only hdr_len+ETH_HLEN before unicast_4addr_packet->subtype/src are read at lines 993-1000 - those reads ARE guarded. The unguarded read is therefore only the 1-byte packet_type at offset 0, which the 2-byte entry pull covers, so the out-of-bounds read is NOT reachable via this line alone. Counterevidence checked: (a) batadv_batman_skb_recv pskb_may_pull(skb,2) at main.c:452 guarantees offsets 0-1 linear; (b) packet_type is byte 0; (c) version byte 1 is checked in main.c:473; (d) all later struct reads (lines 971, 994, 1020 area) are preceded by batadv_check_unicast_packet pskb_may_pull(hdr_size) (routing.c:447) and batadv_check_unicast_ttvn pskb_may_pull(hdr_len+ETH_HLEN) (routing.c:798) plus skb_cow; (e) batadv_recv_my_icmp_packet/batadv_recv_icmp_ttl_exceeded similarly read only after batadv_recv_icmp_packet's pskb_may_pull(hdr_size) (routing.c:350). Mechanism if the entry pull were absent would be a slab OOB read past the linear head of a non-linear received skb; as written, the observable defect is the pre-pull dereference pattern (pointer into linear area used before presence guaranteed), which is exactly the branch invariant even though the concrete byte is within the 2-byte guarantee.

Untrusted source: batadv_route_unicast_packet() is reached from batadv_recv_unicast_packet()/batadv_recv_unhandled_unicast_packet() (routing.c:928, 1028) for any received unicast batman frame. Checks before use: its callers did pskb_may_pull(hdr_size) via batadv_check_unicast_packet (hdr_size >= sizeof(struct batadv_unicast_packet) = 10) and pskb_may_pull(hdr_len + ETH_HLEN) in batadv_check_unicast_ttvn (routing.c:798), so unicast_packet->ttl (offset 2) and ->dest (offset 4, ETH_ALEN bytes) reads are within pulled linear bytes for the normal UNICAST path. However, batadv_recv_unhandled_unicast_packet sets hdr_size = sizeof(struct batadv_unicast_packet) too, so both paths pull at least 10 bytes before routing. Counterevidence: skb_cow in check_unicast_ttvn re-cows but does not shrink headlen; no read in this function exceeds the 10-byte header that callers guarantee. ethhdr = eth_hdr(skb) at line 659 reads the mac header which eth_type_trans keeps linear by construction. So the ttl/dest reads are guarded by caller pulls; remaining concern is only the pattern of re-deriving the pointer after skb_cow (which the code does correctly at line 685-686).

Untrusted source: xt_osf_match() runs in the receive-side iptables xt_osf match on every SYN TCP packet whose IP options/TCP doff the attacker controls. Missing guarantee: the return of skb_header_pointer() is never NULL-checked (scanner over all 253 skb_header_pointer sites in net/ and drivers/net/ flagged only this site plus __skb_header_pointer uses in flow_dissector that are all guarded by 'if (!doff) return' / 'if (ports) return *ports'). Unsafe use: on a non-linear skb whose TCP options (attacker-chosen doff>5, optsize = doff*4 - 20) lie in frags/fraglist, skb_header_pointer() returns NULL; optp stays NULL, _optp is NULL, and the loop at line 261 dereferences *optp (lines 262, 268, 270, 272) -> NULL-pointer read / crash inside the softirq xt match. Guard against false positive: the NULL dereference requires a configured xt_osf rule plus a loaded fingerprint whose summed option lengths equal the attacker's optsize (foptsize == optsize, foptsize <= MAX_IPOPTLEN, totlen == f->ss, TTL window match) so matching must pass first, and the skb must actually be non-linear at the match hook - which packet-local hooks (PRE_ROUTING/LOCAL_IN) allow for GRO/SG/aggregated frames. Counterevidence checked: if the bytes are linear the pointer is valid and only the pattern matches; the deref is a read of NULL (not the seed's UAF), which the branch definition explicitly treats as the same missing-linear-guarantee invariant.

Untrusted source: batadv_recv_unicast_packet is reached via the batman-adv ptype handler batadv_batman_skb_recv (main.c:415) on any mesh-attached interface, from remote-originated ethernet frames. Missing guarantee: the code casts skb->data to a 20-byte (4addr) struct and reads unicast_packet->packet_type BEFORE any pull in this function - the entry dispatcher (main.c:441) only guarantees pskb_may_pull(skb, 2), i.e. two bytes of linear data. The read at line 955 (packet_type, byte 0) is inside those 2 bytes, but the follow-on reads - unicast_packet->dest (bytes 4-9) at line 975 and unicast_4addr_packet->subtype (byte 15) / src at line 977 - happen after batadv_check_unicast_packet (line 961) has done pskb_may_pull(skb, hdr_size=10 or 20), so the deeper reads are guarded by the pull (assuming a non-linear skb makes the pull really linearize: pskb_may_pull does guarantee headlen >= hdr_size on success). The unguarded byte is only packet_type at offset 0, covered by the caller's 2-byte pull, and version at main.c:462 also covered. So the pattern matches the branch but the concrete out-of-bounds read is not established for this s02 variant. This is the same site family that Fact f005 reported for s01 at medium confidence; here the deep-read path is verified guarded.

ieee80211_process_tdls_channel_switch() is a mac80211 receive-path handler fed by over-the-air TDLS action frames (network-received sk_buff, attacker-craftable frame content). It captures tf as a cast of skb->data at line 2010, calls skb_linearize(skb) at line 2020 (comment says 'we want to access the entire packet'), and then dereferences the stale tf->action_code at line 2026 without re-deriving tf. skb_linearize() on a non-linear skb calls __pskb_linearize -> pskb_expand_head, which frees the old head, so the pre-linearize pointer is dangling - the exact missing-refetch invariant of the phonet pep_get_sb seed (pointer derived from skb data used across an operation that may reallocate the head). The 'packet/size was already validated by mac80211 Rx path' comment validates size only, not pointer liveness. Counterevidence checked: the surrounding handler does not reassign tf anywhere between 2020 and 2026, and no pskb_may_pull precedes the capture that would make the use safe; reachability requires a driver delivering a non-linear RX skb into mac80211 (SG/GRO RX), which is driver-dependent and not verified here.

ieee80211_invoke_fast_rx() handles received wifi data frames (network-received sk_buff with attacker-controlled header fields). hdr is captured as a cast of skb->data at line 5010 and used at 5044/5047/5059/5062 before any pull. The non-mesh non-AMSDU path then calls pskb_may_pull(skb, snap_offs + sizeof(*payload)) at line 5077; pskb_may_pull can call __pskb_pull_tail which allocates a new data buffer and moves skb->data. payload is correctly refetched at 5080, but hdr is NOT refetched, and hdr->frame_control is dereferenced again at line 5106 (plus hdr->addr1/2/3 for the addrs copy further down in the same function) after the pull and after pskb_trim(skb, skb->len - fast_rx->icv_len) at line 5103. On a non-linear RX frame whose SNAP header lies beyond skb_headlen, the pull reallocates the head and hdr becomes a dangling pointer into freed memory. Counterevidence checked: pskb_trim/___pskb_trim itself never pulls or reallocates the head (it only drops tail bytes/frags), so the concrete realloc source is the pskb_may_pull at 5077; the function never reassigns hdr. Reachability requires a driver delivering non-linear skbs with hdrlen bytes linear but snap_offs+8 bytes in frags, which is driver-dependent and unverified.

mt7925_mcu_rx_event() captures rxd as a cast of skb->data at line 642, calls skb_linearize(skb) at line 644, and only afterwards dereferences the stale rxd->option at line 647. skb_linearize() reallocates the head exactly when the skb is non-linear, making rxd dangling - a literal mirror of the seed's capture-before-pull shape, with the dereference used to steer kernel control flow (solicited vs unsolicited event dispatch). The skb source is the mediatek WiFi firmware/DMA event path, not a remote network packet, and mt76 typically builds MCU event skbs linearly (in which case skb_linearize returns 0 without reallocating and rxd stays valid); the non-linear precondition and attacker influence on event bytes were not verified, hence low confidence.

Untrusted source: GARP PDU bytes received on a bridge port reach garp_pdu_rcv() (802.2 LLC/stp receive path) and garp_pdu_parse_attr() reads the attacker-chosen length byte ga->len straight from the PDU. Violated invariant: ga is a pointer into the skb linear head captured at line 449 and then used after pskb_may_pull(skb, ga->len) at line 453; on a non-linear skb (payload in frags, headlen < ga->len) pskb_may_pull()->__pskb_pull_tail() can allocate a new head buffer and free the old one, so ga dangles — exactly the seed's validated-then-invalidated pointer mechanism. Unsafe use: stale ga is dereferenced after the pull at lines 455/456 (ga->len), 461 (ga->event), and 485 (garp_attr_lookup(app, ga->data, dlen, attrtype) reads dlen bytes from the freed old head). Impact: slab use-after-free read on packet reception (expected KASAN 'slab-use-after-free in garp_pdu_parse_attr'), stale/freed-memory contents copied into GARP attribute state, and crash. Counterevidence checked: if the skb is fully linear the pull is a no-op and ga stays valid, so the bug requires an attacker-crafted non-linear GARP skb (scatter-gather RX, GRO, or L2 tunnel decap into a bridge port) — reachable in principle but not dynamically reproduced here; the sibling MRP parser (net/802/mrp.c) refetches via skb_header_pointer/uses skb_copy_bits and does not share this flaw.

rt_mt6() (ip6t_rt.c:36) is an xtables packet-match handler invoked on the netfilter receive path with attacker-controlled packets; an IPv6 routing extension header can arrive in an skb whose bytes live only in frags (GRO/scatter-gather), so nothing pulls those bytes into the linear head. The earlier skb_header_pointer for rh (line 56) IS NULL-checked, and the two loop uses (lines 130, 163) are NULL-checked, but the IP6T_RT_RES branch assigns rp at line 106 and immediately does 'ret = (*rp == 0)' at line 112 with no NULL test. skb_header_pointer returns NULL when the requested 4 bytes are not in the linear head, so a crafted non-linear IPv6 packet carrying a routing header plus an iptables '-m rt --rt-res' rule yields a NULL-pointer read in the match hook. Counterevidence checked: 'skb->len - ptr < hdrlen' at line 67 bounds only the logical length, not linear presence; no pskb_may_pull/skb_linearize exists anywhere in rt_mt6; no other deref of rp exists.

nf_osf_hdr_ctx_init() (nfnetlink_osf.c:166) is reached from nf_osf_match()/nf_osf_find(), the xt_osf and nft_osf passive-OS-fingerprint matches on the receive path. tcp->doff (a 4-bit packet field) can claim up to 60 bytes of TCP header; when ip_hdrlen(skb)+20+optsize bytes are not all in the linear head (non-linear skb from GRO/frags), skb_header_pointer returns NULL and ctx->optp stays NULL, yet nf_osf_match_one() later does 'if (f->opt[optnum].kind == *ctx->optp)' (line 99) after only a ctx->optsize == foptsize comparison, with no NULL check anywhere. The bytes whose presence was validated (the tcph doff used to size the fetch) and the bytes actually used (optp) are the same region, but presence in the linear area is never guaranteed. Counterevidence: the deref only happens when a fingerprint with matching optsize exists in the loaded osf table; when doff<=5, ctx->optp is also NULL but ctx->optsize==0 short-circuits at lines 92-93, so the NULL deref needs doff>5 plus a fingerprint whose foptsize equals the attacker-chosen optsize.

Untrusted source: packets traversing the Bluetooth 6LoWPAN/IPSP netdev reach bt_xmit()/send_pkt(); remote peers can induce locally generated IPv6 traffic (ICMPv6/NDP replies) on this interface. Violated invariant: send_pkt() stores the skb pointer into channel-lifetime state at line 438 ('chan->data = skb;', comment 'Remember the skb so that we can send EAGAIN to the caller') without transferring ownership; bt_xmit() then unconditionally calls dev_kfree_skb(skb) at line 538 after send_pkt() returns, so chan->data retains a pointer to the freed sk_buff for the life of the l2cap_chan; send_mcast_pkt() (lines 479-488) repeats this per peer via local_skb followed by kfree_skb(local_skb). Unsafe use: any later reader of chan->data for an IPSP channel would dereference freed slab memory. Counterevidence checked: grep over net/bluetooth shows no reader of chan->data in 6lowpan.c (only the writer at 438) and the readers in l2cap_sock.c/smp.c/a2mp.c belong to socket/SMP/AMP channels, so the dangling pointer is currently latent; reported as a hypothesis with low confidence, no exploit claim.

lec_start_xmit() saves lec_h = (struct lecdatahdr_8023 *)skb->data at net/atm/lec.c:244. On the short-frame path, when skb->len + skb_tailroom < LEC_MINIMUM_8023_SIZE, skb_copy_expand() at :263 builds a new skb and dev_kfree_skb(skb) at :266 frees the original head, so lec_h is dangling. The stale pointer is then unconditionally dereferenced: dst = lec_h->h_dest at :278 is fed into lec_arp_resolve() at :280, and lec_h->h_dest is printed at :286, :290, :302 (pr_debug only). The free is inside the same function (no helper trace needed), the skb is attacker-influenced data on the LANE netdev TX path (frame length attacker-chosen), and no re-derivation of lec_h from the new skb2 occurs. Counterevidence checked: the non-expanding path (enough tailroom) leaves lec_h valid, and the headroom-expansion path at :227-241 reassigns skb=skb2 before skb_push, so only the skb_copy_expand branch is affected.

send_pkt() stores the skb pointer into long-lived l2cap channel state: chan->data = skb at net/bluetooth/6lowpan.c:515 (comment 'Remember the skb so that we can send EAGAIN to the caller if we run out of credits'). bt_xmit() frees that skb via dev_kfree_skb(skb) at :622 (and send_mcast_pkt kfree_skb at :573) without clearing chan->data. The l2cap core then invokes the channel callbacks on remote-driven events: chan->ops->suspend(chan) at net/bluetooth/l2cap_core.c:1270 and :2484 (LE flow-control credit exhaustion) and chan->ops->resume(chan) at :5579 (credits received) and :7414 (encryption change, i.e. attacker-supplied HCI traffic). chan_suspend_cb()/chan_resume_cb() at 6lowpan.c:965-987 reload struct sk_buff *skb = chan->data (:967/:979) and WRITE lowpan_cb(skb)->status = -EAGAIN at :974 / = 0 at :986, i.e. a 4-byte write into skb->cb of the freed skb. IPSP channels are created with chan->mode = L2CAP_MODE_LE_FLOWCTL at 6lowpan.c:743, so the suspend/resume path is exactly the one that stores chan->data. Counterevidence checked: chan->data is never re-derived or cleared anywhere in 6lowpan.c; the only other readers are these two callbacks; the window is per-channel 'last skb sent', so the UAF write only lands when the remote peer triggers suspend/resume/encryption after the freed skb.

send_pkt() stores the skb pointer into long-lived l2cap channel state (chan->data = skb, net/bluetooth/6lowpan.c:447, with the comment 'Remember the skb'), and both callers then free the skb: the unicast path bt_xmit() calls send_pkt(lowpan_cb(skb)->chan, skb, netdev) at net/bluetooth/6lowpan.c:541 and dev_kfree_skb(skb) at :549; the multicast path send_mcast_pkt() calls send_pkt(pentry->chan, local_skb, netdev) at :498 then kfree_skb(local_skb) at :501. After those frees, chan->data is a dangling skb pointer that lives until the next send_pkt overwrites it or the channel closes. l2cap_chan_send() itself takes no reference on the skb (it copies out of skb->data via the kvec at :449-450), so ownership definitively returns to the xmit path. I searched all readers of chan->data in net/bluetooth/ (grep 'chan->data'): every other reader is in net/bluetooth/l2cap_sock.c, where chan->data holds a struct sock * for socket-backed channels; for the 6lowpan IPSP channel (ops = bt_6lowpan_chan_ops, no .teardown of chan->data, chan_create() never initializes chan->data to NULL explicitly before use and l2cap_sock readers are never invoked for 6lowpan ops), no dereference of the stale skb pointer was found in this snapshot, so no crash or disclosure is proven - this is the stored-dangling-pointer shape (branch pattern 2), reported as a latent UAF hypothesis with low confidence, mirroring facts f004/f026 which found the identical store in s01/s02.

Pattern-2 store of skb pointer into longer-lived per-channel state: send_pkt() (net/bluetooth/6lowpan.c:438-447) executes `chan->data = skb;` (line 447) for the IPSP l2cap channel while the skb is only borrowed, and the skb->data-derived kvec is built at line 449 (iv.iov_base = skb->data). The caller bt_xmit() unconditionally runs `dev_kfree_skb(skb);` at net/bluetooth/6lowpan.c:549 after send_pkt() returns, dropping the last reference, so chan->data becomes a dangling skb pointer that persists in channel state after every unicast TX. A later l2cap_sock.c style dereference of chan->data (l2cap_sock.c uses chan->data as `struct sock *` for normal L2CAP channels) would be a UAF; however in this snapshot I found no reader that dereferences chan->data for the 6lowpan IPSP channel (all chan->data readers found are in net/bluetooth/l2cap_sock.c and hci_conn/hci_core, which operate on `data_q`, a different field, or on socket channels, and lowpan_chan_ops has no callback that reads chan->data back). The untrusted source is attacker-supplied IPv6/6LoWPAN traffic via the bt6lowpan interface (ndo_start_xmit), the free is concrete and verbatim, and the stored pointer is the concrete use-shaped hazard, so I report it as a hypothesis with low confidence: a latent dangling skb pointer with no in-tree dereference demonstrated in s04.

Untrusted source: an Ethernet frame transmitted on a LANE emulated LAN device arrives from the network stack with attacker-influenced header content and length. Save: line 247 caches lec_h = (struct lecdatahdr_8023 *)skb->data and line 248 writes through it. Free/ownership transfer: when the frame is shorter than LEC_MINIMUM_8023_SIZE and lacks tailroom (attacker-chosen small frame), lines 266-269 skb_copy_expand() into a new skb and dev_kfree_skb(skb) free the original head while line 274 rebinds only the local skb variable; lec_h is never refetched (compare the explicit fix pattern in net/ax25/ax25_ip.c:152-162 which re-derives bp after kfree_skb). Unsafe use: line 281 dst = lec_h->h_dest, lines 289/293 lec_h->h_dest in pr_debug, and line 305 lec_h->h_dest in the tx_wait drain loop all dereference the dangling pointer after the free, giving a slab use-after-free read (and an input value, the destination MAC, taken from freed memory drives lec_arp_resolve routing). Counterevidence checked: if skb_copy_expand fails the function returns before any use; when no expansion occurs lec_h stays valid, so the UAF is conditional on the short-frame path (skb->len < 60 with insufficient tailroom), which is why confidence is not 'certain' at runtime; the frees at 295/309 happen after the last dereference. Impact: remote-triggerable UAF read and possibly wrong-VCC forwarding of attacker frames on LANE (CONFIG_ATM + lane module), reachable by sending a short frame through a lec0 device.

Untrusted source: the 802.11 header carried in the transmitted skb is attacker-influenced (locally generated or forwarded frames). Save: line 825 hdr = (void *)skb->data inside iwl_mvm_tx_tso_segment(). Ownership transfer/free: line 836 skb_gso_segment() consumes/frees the input skb and returns a list of new segmented skbs; line 841 consume_skb(skb) then drops the last reference, so hdr points into freed head memory. Unsafe use: line 864 ieee80211_is_data_qos(hdr->frame_control) inside the per-segment loop reads the 802.11 frame_control field through the stale pointer after the free, so a segmented A-MSDU frame whose first subframe is short (tcp_payload_len <= mss) dereferences freed memory and uses the stale bit to decide whether to strip the A-MSDU-present QoS bit. Counterevidence checked: the same hdr is captured again independently in iwl_mvm_tx_tso() at line 899, which is a separate function and separate skb lifetime, so only the iwl_mvm_tx_tso_segment copy is affected; ip_base_id (line 831) is saved by value before the free and is safe. Limitations: triggering requires hardware/software GSO segmentation to actually segment (gso_size set, A-MSDU-capable station), and no build/KASAN run was possible to empirically confirm skb_gso_segment always frees the original head (when it returns NULL, i.e. no segmentation, the skb is kept and hdr stays valid), hence medium confidence.

Untrusted source: a CAN/CAN-FD frame sent on a vxcan tunnel whose CAN header (including the len field) is fully attacker-chosen via an unprivileged PF_CAN socket. Save: line 39 cfd = (struct canfd_frame *)skb->data. Ownership transfer and free: line 53 can_create_echo_skb(skb) (include/linux/can/skb.h:62) frees the original skb with consume_skb(skb) whenever the frame is shared (loopback-echo clones, can skb owners set by the CAN stack) and returns a clone with a different head, and line 63 netif_rx_ni(skb) hands the skb to the peer netdevice's receive queue, after which it can be consumed at any time by the peer. Unsafe use: lines 65 and 68 read cfd->len (srcstats->tx_bytes / peerstats->rx_bytes) after both the potential free and the netif_rx handoff, so the statistics byte count is taken from freed or foreign-owned memory. Counterevidence checked: can_dropped_invalid_skb() at line 42 validates the frame length before the pointer is saved, but nothing revalidates the pointer after the ownership changes; the unshared fast path (no clone) leaves cfd pointing into skb head that is still allocated when netif_rx_ni queues it, but once handed to the backlog the bytes may be consumed before line 65 runs, so the handoff case alone is still a lifetime violation. Impact is limited to wrong byte accounting plus the underlying UAF read of a freed slab head.

Untrusted source: any remote IPv6 packet carrying an SRH (routing header type 4) reaching ipv6_rthdr_rcv. The caller ipv6_rthdr_rcv (net/ipv6/exthdrs.c:660-668) does pskb_may_pull(skb, transport_offset+8) and pskb_may_pull(skb, transport_offset+((skb_transport_header(skb)[1]+1)<<3)), so the SRH bytes ARE guaranteed linear before ipv6_srh_rcv is called; the plain missing-linearization half of the branch does not apply. The violated invariant is the transferable seed rule: a pointer derived from the skb data area (hdr = skb_transport_header(skb), line 375) must be re-derived after any call that can reallocate or free the skb head. Between capture (line 375) and the dereferences at lines 396-425 (hdr->segments_left, hdr->nexthdr, hdr->hdrlen) the function calls seg6_hmac_validate_skb(skb) (line 389, under CONFIG_IPV6_SEG6_HMAC) and seg6_hmac_compute, which hash srh with crypto_shash_setkey/update/final on a struct scatterlist-free linear walk; no pull/trim/expand runs there in this tree (net/ipv6/seg6_hmac.c:236-277 contains no pskb_may_pull/skb_cow/pskb_expand_head/skb_trim), so the stale-pointer half is NOT triggered on that path. Counterevidence checked: the classic reallocating path is skb_cloned() -> pskb_expand_head() at lines 433-442, and the code explicitly re-derives hdr = (struct ipv6_sr_hdr *)skb_transport_header(skb) at line 441 after the expand, so that site is correct; the looped_back re-entry at line 475-482 re-derives hdr via skb_transport_header after __skb_pull too. The concrete defect that remains: hdr is captured at 375 BEFORE the seg6_hmac_validate_skb() call at 389 and only re-derived at 441; if any future/optional path inside the HMAC validation (or any helper inserted there) linearizes/unshares the skb, hdr dangles exactly like the seed's ph after pskb_may_pull. Additionally, on the decap branch (lines 397-419) hdr->nexthdr and hdr->hdrlen are read after skb_pull(skb, offset) at 402 (data moved forward), which is not itself a head realloc. So this is a validated-equals-used pattern (the pull guarantee was established once, at caller scope, and the accessor-derived pointer is not re-derived across a validation call), reported per the instruction to report the shared-pattern hypothesis with uncertainty; it is NOT a confirmed KASAN UAF.
